STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u3

(u0, at_exit) -> u3
(u0, box_fell & !at_exit) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, at_exit) -> u3
(u1, holding_box & !at_exit) -> u0
(u1, !holding_box & !at_exit) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, at_exit) -> u3
(u2, holding_box & !at_exit) -> u0
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, else) -> u3
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u1, holding_box & !at_exit, u0) -> 0.2
(u2, holding_box & !at_exit, u0) -> 0.05
(u0, at_exit, u3) -> 1.0
(u1, at_exit, u3) -> 1.0
(u2, at_exit, u3) -> 1.0
feedback: The machine correctly encodes the preference task and passes all checks. Semantic fidelity: each `box_fell` event opens a one-step prompt window (u1); a pickup on the very next labeling fires (u1, holding_box & !at_exit) -> u0 with 0.2, while any later pickup goes u1 -> u2 -> u0 with 0.05, so prompt (1.2 total) > late (1.05) > no pickup (1.0) preserves the 'preferably on the next move' ordering, and the return to u0 after every pickup handles 'each time' (the schedule allows at most two falls). Event/condition distinction is right: `box_fell` is used as an edge trigger into u1 and `holding_box` as a state guard; the fall step itself earns nothing, and the pickup-on-due-step case (action first, then events) is handled correctly because `holding_box` is false on that labeling, so the machine still lands in u1. Coverage: guards in every state are mutually exclusive and exhaustive (at_exit / holding_box / complement), so siren_ringing and switch_toggled are absorbed without trapping the machine; the u1 else self-loop is unreachable because the three explicit guards already partition the space, and the `!at_exit` conjuncts are redundant given the environment constraints (box_fell/at_exit never co-occur), but both are harmless defensive choices since at_exit is tested first in each state's order. Reachability and compactness: all four states are reachable, u3 is entered only via at_exit, which matches the last-step-only semantics of that proposition and makes it a proper accepting sink; FINAL_STATES header is present, nonempty, and declares u3, which also appears in STATES. Reward safety: progress rewards are event-based and bounded (at most two falls, so at most 0.4 progress plus the 1.0 terminal); no farming is possible because deliberate drops never emit box_fell, empty-handed due falls are skipped, and toggling earns nothing. The flat 1.0 exit from u1/u2 is defensible under the 'preferably' phrasing since the base objective is the exit and the preference is carried entirely by the differentiated pickup rewards. Format matches the paper's flattened RM schema exactly (REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES headers, (s, formula) -> s' transitions, (s, formula, s') -> r rewards, formulas over only the five propositions). No revision needed.
